traits: Sticky, shiny, smooth cap, up to 12 cm, yellowish beige to reddish brown, often evenly coloured
Adnate tubes, pale yellow then olive-yellow; evenly coloured pores that weep milky drops at first
Stem about 10 × 2 cm, yellowish with opalescent droplets, then yellower and dotted at the top with brown or russet granules; no ring
Yellowish-white flesh, slightly sour · spicy smell
Orange-brown spores with an olive sheen
safetyNote: Its sticky skin is laxative. ANSES attributes digestive upset to it, often with trembling, headaches and anxiety, a few hours after the meal: 25 cases recorded in France between 1999 and 2015. No cooking is shown to be effective. Skin contact can also cause dermatitis. The Swiss controllers list it among edible species while asking for the cap skin to be removed, and the German mycological society also lists it as edible: the most cautious status is kept.
